content.title: Complete guest checkout on a phone with a valid weekday delivery date
content.intent: Prove that a visitor can complete the end-to-end bouquet checkout as a guest on a phone-sized web surface, choose a non-Sunday delivery date, and reach an order confirmation that includes an order number.
content.technique_notes: Derived from covering_array strength=3 over surface × checkout_mode × delivery_date because money risk applied; the tool returned two unique combinations and this scenario covers the valid non-Sunday combination. Applied the stateful-flow and web-form profiles because the source described an end-to-end checkout flow with date selection and completion on a phone. dedupe_candidates found no duplicate candidate, and graph_search_similar_batch found no existing scenario-level reuse candidate.

content.title: Sunday delivery date is unavailable during guest checkout on a phone
content.intent: Prove that the delivery-date control in the phone-sized guest checkout flow forbids selecting a Sunday.
content.technique_notes: Derived from covering_array strength=3 over surface × checkout_mode × delivery_date because money risk applied; the tool returned two unique combinations and this scenario covers the Sunday-forbidden combination. Applied negative and web-form techniques because the source stated a specific forbidden date choice rather than an alternate successful outcome. dedupe_candidates found no duplicate candidate, and graph_search_similar_batch found no existing scenario-level reuse candidate.

judgements.rationale: [value_score] Scored highest because it is the only path that proves the business outcome of captured self-service orders and it exercises the most high-risk promises in one grounded journey.
[value_score] Scored second because it proves the explicit Sunday exclusion rule, which prevents orders that Sarah cannot fulfill, but it does not by itself prove the full purchase completes.
